title: Cross-Wrist Ride
description: A ride from turtle/side where the attacker controls both wrists, stretching the opponent arms to expose the back.
topPlayerGoals: The top player wants to control Cross-Wrist Ride through head position, inside position, and directed pressure.
Hold both wrists, maintain chest pressure, and open a hook entry.
Keep a stable base so you are not off-balanced or countered.
bottomPlayerGoals: The bottom player wants to survive Cross-Wrist Ride with frames, pummeling, or the right angle.
Pull both arms back to the body, build a base, and prevent shoulder-line separation.
Recognize danger signals early instead of waiting for the position to settle.
controlPoints: Main control point: Both wrists controlled, chest-on-back connection, and knee ride angle..
Head, hands, hips, and knees should share the same force direction.
The elbow-knee connection or hip-shoulder line determines whether the position is still alive or already locked.
escapePriorities: Escape priority: Bring elbows to ribs before pulling arms in — do not pull straight to the chest..
Protect the neck, back, knee line, or arm line before countering.
If inside position is lost, reset one defensive layer first.

advancementOptions.action: Transition to hook seatbelt or body triangle
advancementOptions.why: This is the natural branch when you win the main control point and the opponent is forced to defend.

dangerSignals: The chin or neck is pulled out of a safe line.
The elbow separates from the ribs or knee.
The hip line is locked while the shoulder line is still being pulled.
You need a long hand post to avoid falling.
